title: DebianPolicyDeltaReviewV1
description:
The 1D.2 policy-delta report.

The 1D.2 RED commit's struct is the *minimal* shape: just `schema_version`, `report_kind`, `verdict`, `diagnostics`, plus the three core fields (`candidate_standards_version`, `baseline_standards_version`, and `comparison_outcome`). The 1D.2 GREEN commit's struct extends the same shape with the §22 comprehensive fields (the `diagnostics` carries the `E_POLICY_BASELINE_STALE` line, the `comparison_outcome` is the `AboveBaseline` / `AtBaseline` / `BelowBaseline` tri-state).

baseline_standards_version.description: The manifest's `baseline_policy_version` (currently `"4.7.4.1"`). Always present when the manifest loaded successfully.

candidate_standards_version.description: The candidate's declared `Standards-Version` from `debian/control`. `None` when the field is absent (Policy-violation, but the report records the absence — `verdict: "fail"` with `E_STANDARDS_VERSION_MISSING`).

comparison_outcome.description: The §22 comparison outcome. `None` when one or both `Standards-Version` values are missing.

diagnostics.description: Per-check failure / informational lines. Empty when `verdict` is `pass`.

provenance.description: The candidate's BLAKE3 fingerprint, Git commit, and Git tree; the inspector binary's version. 1C.2's `Provenance` type, reused.

Diagnostic.description: A single failure or informational line from the tool.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable error code, e.g. `E_DEBIAN_DIR_MISSING`. Future tools can match on this without parsing the message.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. The tool does not embed the offending value (a) to keep PII out of the report and (b) so the same diagnostic text can serve any fixture.

path.description: The on-disk path that triggered the diagnostic, when applicable (e.g. `debian/`, `debian/changelog`).

Provenance.description:
The provenance block (§18 provenance group).

The candidate fingerprint, Git commit, and Git tree are the candidate's identity (the §18 lines 842-846 requirement). `inspector_version` is the version of the `ironmaint-debian-tool` binary that produced the report, so a downstream consumer can tell which parser version emitted the report.

StandardsVersionComparison.description:
The §22 Standards-Version comparison outcome.

`AboveBaseline` is the gate-triggering case: the candidate declares a `Standards-Version` newer than the manifest's `baseline_policy_version`, so the candidate cannot be evaluated against the adapter's known Policy and the §22 gate is blocked. `AtBaseline` and `BelowBaseline` are both pass-path cases (the candidate's declared version is known).

oneOf.description: The candidate's `Standards-Version` is strictly newer than the manifest's `baseline_policy_version`. The §22 gate is blocked; the verdict is `Fail`.
The candidate's `Standards-Version` equals the manifest's `baseline_policy_version`. The candidate is at the manifest's known Policy; the verdict is `Pass`.
The candidate's `Standards-Version` is strictly older than the manifest's `baseline_policy_version`. The candidate is within the manifest's known Policy; the verdict is `Pass`.

At least one §17 check failed (mismatched name, mismatched version, unparsable `debian/control`, unparsable `debian/changelog`, missing `debian/`, unidentifiable source format, unparsable mandatory metadata). Diagnostics list the specific failure.

The tool could not establish the fact at all: the workspace path is unreadable, an IO error occurred, a parser binary is missing. The §17 rule "parser binary missing → InfrastructureError" lives here.
